data:
One Dark Factory instance is one Helm release: a control plane, a gateway and one PostgreSQL database, serving one tenant. Agents run in sandbox pods, one pod per run, in a namespace of their own. The rest of this page lists the components; Agent runs follows one run through them.
flowchart TB B["Browser"] -->|HTTPS| CP subgraph inst["Instance namespace"] direction LR CP["Control plane"] -->|PolicyWatch| GW["Gateway"] end subgraph sbx["Sandbox namespace"] SB["Sandbox pod
runtime + harness"] --- PVC[("Task volume")] end SB -->|agent channel| CP SB -->|proxy, Git| GW CP --> DB[("PostgreSQL")] CP -->|API| FORGE["Forge"] GW -->|Git| FORGE GW --> EXT["Allowed hosts"]
data.components#Components: Component Runs as Does Holds Control plane Deployment dark-factory serve Web UI, task and run scheduling, the agent channel for sandboxes, forge plugins, sandbox provisioning, policy distribution to the gateway The database connection; resolves credentials from Secret references when it uses them Gateway Deployment dark-factory gateway (2 or more replicas) Egress proxy for sandbox HTTP(S), Git smart-HTTP proxy with push checks, live traffic events No database access and no Kubernetes token; policies and forge credentials arrive from the control plane and stay in memory migrate job Helm pre-install and pre-upgrade hook Schema migrations, application role and grants The owner role’s password Sandbox pod Pod per run in the sandbox namespace, Kata Containers where configured The project image with the runtime (factory-agent) and the harness (for example Claude Code over ACP) mounted as image volumes The task volume at /data; the harness credential in memory PostgreSQL External All state: projects, personas, tasks, runs, transcripts and their binary content, requests, egress rules, audit log The control plane and the gateway are the same binary in two modes. The control plane can run with several replicas: every replica serves the UI and agent connections and can start runs (the database prevents two runs of one task); jobs that must run once, such as the task volume cleanup, run on the replica holding the instance lease.
data.connections#Connections: From To Protocol Authentication Browser Control plane :8080 HTTPS through your ingress or Gateway API route OIDC login, server-side session Sandbox Control plane :9443 (agent port) gRPC, bidirectional stream mTLS: a per-pod certificate from cert-manager’s CSI driver, checked against the pod’s IP and UID Sandbox Gateway :3128 (proxy) HTTP CONNECT and plain HTTP proxying Source pod IP, looked up in the sandbox registry Sandbox Gateway :8443 (Git) Git smart HTTP over HTTPS (instance CA) Source pod IP; the path names the task Gateway Control plane :9444 (internal) gRPC (PolicyWatch, push records, events) mTLS Control plane Gateway :9444 (internal) gRPC Tail for the live traffic view mTLS Control plane Forge API HTTPS from a forge plugin The project’s forge credential, added by the control plane Gateway Forge Git HTTPS The project’s forge credential, injected by the Git proxy Sandboxes resolve no DNS names: the proxy and control plane addresses are passed as IPs, and the generated NetworkPolicy of each run allows only the control plane, the gateway and explicitly allowed cluster services. Details: Security.
data.design-records#Design records: The decisions behind this layout are recorded as ADRs in the repository, for example ADR-0029 (egress gateway), ADR-0030 (Kubernetes only) and ADR-0013 (single-tenant instances).
data.kubernetes-footprint#Kubernetes footprin: Namespace Contains Created by Instance (for example dark-factory) Control plane, gateway, migrate job, Services, Secrets with credentials, Leases the Helm release Sandbox (for example dark-factory-sandboxes) Sandbox pods, task volumes (PVCs), generated per-run NetworkPolicies the chart (sandboxNamespace.create) or you; never the control plane The control plane gets the permissions it needs in these two namespaces only: pods, PVCs and NetworkPolicies in the sandbox namespace; leases, Secrets (read) and EndpointSlices in the instance namespace. The gateway and sandbox pods get no Kubernetes API token. At startup the control plane checks its permissions and refuses to start if one is missing.

data: A task is a unit of work for one persona in one project. A run is one sandbox lifetime that works on a task: it starts when the task has something to do (a new task, a message, a resume time that passed) and ends when the agent is done, waits too long for an answer, or is stopped. A task usually has several runs. Its code lives in Git, on the branch factory/task/; the task volume only caches the checkout between runs.
data.continuation-across-runs#Continuation ac: Every run after the first gets the harness session id of the previous run and a summary of the task’s transcript: title, description, user messages, agent messages and one line per tool call, capped in size. A harness that can resume its session (Claude Code) continues it; others start from the summary. The workspace comes from the task branch, the WIP snapshot and the cached checkout on the task volume.
data.how-a-run-ends#How a run ends: Outcome Task status afterwards completed (the agent called complete_task) in_review; the pull request is marked ready and gets the completion summary end_turn (idle deadline passed) waiting blocked (a blocking question was not answered in time) blocked rate_limited (the model provider’s usage limit) rate_limited, with a resume time; the next run starts automatically and continues limit_reached (a budget, or the harness’s token or turn limit) limit_reached sandbox_lost, connect_timeout, provisioning_failed queued again with a growing delay, up to runs.maxAutoResumes (default 3) times; then failed cancelled (stopped by a human, or over the wall-clock budget) waiting; a cancelled task stays cancelled, a task marked done stays completed failed failed If messages are still undelivered at the end of a run, the task becomes queued instead, so the next run picks them up.
data.one-run#One run: sequenceDiagram autonumber participant UI as Web UI / DB participant CP as Control plane participant K as Kubernetes participant R as Runtime (sandbox) participant H as Harness participant G as Gateway participant F as Forge UI->>CP: task queued (new task or message) CP->>K: task volume task-, sandbox pod, NetworkPolicy K-->>CP: pod started (pod IP) R->>CP: connect (mTLS), Hello CP->>R: harness credential, Assign, prompt R->>G: clone or fetch through the Git proxy G->>F: forward with the forge credential R->>H: start session (new or resumed) loop each turn R->>H: prompt H-->>R: updates (messages, tool calls) R->>CP: transcript events R->>G: push factory/task/ (push checks) R->>CP: push report opt first commit ahead of base CP->>F: open draft pull request (plugin) end end Note over CP,R: waits for messages until the idle deadline CP->>R: Release (or Cancel) R->>G: push task branch, WIP snapshot R->>CP: run report (outcome, workspace state) CP->>K: delete pod (volume stays) opt outcome completed CP->>F: mark pull request ready, post the completion summary end Scheduling. A task is due when it is queued (or rate_limited) and its resume time has passed. Up to runs.maxConcurrent runs (default 4) are active at a time; further due tasks wait, oldest first. A task never has two active runs. Provisioning. The control plane ensures the task volume exists, creates the sandbox pod (the project’s image with the runtime and harness mounted read-only, the configured runtime class) and a NetworkPolicy for the run. Connecting. The runtime dials the control plane with its pod certificate. The control plane resolves the certificate to the run, sends the persona’s harness credential (memory only, never in the pod spec) and the Assign: repository URL through the Git proxy, branches, commit identity, system prompt, harness settings, budgets and the continuation of earlier runs (harness session id and a transcript summary). Preparing. The runtime clones or updates the workspace through the Git proxy and writes its own .git/config; anything left on the volume is treated as untrusted. Turns. The harness works on the prompt. Every message and tool call is streamed to the control plane and stored as the task’s transcript. After a turn with new commits the runtime pushes the task branch. The first push ahead of the base branch opens a draft pull request. Waiting. Between turns the run waits for messages. A message queued in the UI reaches the agent at the next turn boundary without a new run. After runs.keepAliveSeconds (default 600) without a message, the control plane releases the run. Finalizing. The runtime stops the harness, pushes the task branch, writes a WIP snapshot of uncommitted files to factory/wip/ and reports the outcome. The control plane deletes the pod; the task volume stays for the next run.
data.task-volumes#Task volumes: Each task has one volume (task-), mounted at /data. It is a cache: committed work is in Git, uncommitted work in the WIP snapshot. Volumes of tasks closed for 7 days, or idle for 30 days, are deleted hourly (volumes.retainAfterCloseSeconds, volumes.idleTtlSeconds); Reset workspace in a task’s status menu deletes one on demand. The next run re-clones.

data:
The web UI logs users in through an OIDC provider. The control plane is a confidential OIDC client (authorization code flow with PKCE, performed server-side). Browsers only get an HTTP-only session cookie; tokens stay on the server. Every UI page requires the role board-member, read from a flat claim of the ID token.
sequenceDiagram participant B as Browser participant C as Control plane participant P as OIDC provider B->>C: GET /tasks (no session) C-->>B: 303 /login?next=/tasks B->>C: GET /login C-->>B: 303 provider /auth (state, nonce, PKCE challenge) B->>P: log in P-->>B: 302 /auth/callback?code&state B->>C: GET /auth/callback C->>P: POST /token (code, PKCE verifier, client secret) P-->>C: ID token (role claim), refresh token C-->>B: 303 /tasks + session cookie Provider guides:
Keycloak: client role board-member in a roles claim. Dex: group board-member in the groups claim.
data.control-plane-settings#Control plane set:
The chart renders the auth section of config.yaml from the oidc.* values (chart README):
Field Helm value Required Default Effect auth.issuerUrl oidc.issuerUrl yes Issuer; /.well-known/openid-configuration is discovered below it on every login, callback and refresh. auth.clientId oidc.clientId yes dark-factory (chart) OIDC client ID. auth.clientSecretFile oidc.existingSecret, oidc.clientSecretKey yes File with the client secret (the chart mounts the Secret at /run/secrets/oidc/client-secret). auth.publicUrl oidc.publicUrl yes Externally visible base URL; the redirect URI is /auth/callback, the post-logout redirect /. Must be https://; plain http:// is accepted only on loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1) for local development, and then the session cookie is sent without Secure. serve refuses any other http:// URL. auth.rolesClaim oidc.rolesClaim no roles Top-level ID token claim with the role list. auth.extraScopes oidc.extraScopes no [] Scopes requested in addition to openid and profile, for example [groups, offline_access] for Dex. Without an auth section (oidc.publicUrl empty) dark-factory serve logs a warning, serves only /healthz, /readyz and /assets/*, and the UI is unavailable.
Roles are read at every login and every token refresh; they are never stored as the source of truth. A role removed at the provider takes effect when the access token expires and is refreshed. Live views (task list, task detail) reconnect at that point, so they stop as well.
data.verify#Verify: Open https:///. You are redirected to the provider and, after login, to /tasks. A user without board-member sees 403 with the message Your account lacks the role board-member. Log out deletes the server-side session and ends the provider session (RP-initiated logout).

data: Dex as the OIDC provider. Dex has no roles: the control plane reads the groups claim instead, so the users who may operate the factory are members of the group board-member. Dex passes the groups on from its connector (for example LDAP or an upstream OIDC provider). How the login works and every control plane setting: Authentication.
data.1-register-the-client#1. Register the cl:
Add a static client to the Dex configuration:
staticClients: - id: dark-factory name: Dark Factory secret: redirectURIs: - https://factory.example.org/auth/callback postLogoutRedirectURIs: - https://factory.example.org/ Store the same secret in the instance namespace:
kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-oidc \ --from-literal=client-secret=''
data.2-provide-the-group#2. Provide the group:
The ID token must contain "groups": ["board-member", …]. Where the group comes from depends on the connector:
Connector Group board-member LDAP an LDAP group named board-member (groupSearch of the connector) OIDC (upstream) the upstream groups claim (insecureEnableGroups: true on the connector) Static passwords groups of the user entry; for tests only The group name must be exactly board-member: the control plane compares the claim values as strings. The GitHub connector names every team group : (for example acme:board-member), so it cannot provide the group; use Keycloak or another connector instead.
data.3-configure-the-control-plane#3. Configu:
Dex returns groups only for the scope groups, and a refresh token only for offline_access. Without a refresh token the session ends when the ID token expires.
oidc: issuerUrl: https://dex.example.org/dex clientId: dark-factory existingSecret: dark-factory-oidc clientSecretKey: client-secret publicUrl: https://factory.example.org rolesClaim: groups extraScopes: [groups, offline_access] issuerUrl must match the issuer of the Dex configuration exactly, including the path. Then check the login as in Verify.
The local development setup (just serve-local, dev/dex.yaml) uses the same settings with static users (development guide).
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause Unregistered redirect_uri at Dex The redirect URI does not match oidc.publicUrl + /auth/callback. 403 for a user in the group groups is missing in the scopes (oidc.extraScopes), the connector does not pass groups, or the group name is not exactly board-member. Login unavailable (502) The control plane cannot reach oidc.issuerUrl, or it differs from the Dex issuer. Logged out when the ID token expires offline_access is missing in oidc.extraScopes.

data: Keycloak as the OIDC provider: a confidential client dark-factory and its client role board-member in a top-level roles claim of the ID token. How the login works and every control plane setting: Authentication.
data.1-create-the-client#1. Create the client:
In the realm of your instance, Clients > Create client:
Setting Value Client type OpenID Connect Client ID dark-factory (auth.clientId) Client authentication On (confidential client) Authentication flow Standard flow only; turn off direct access grants and implicit flow Valid redirect URIs https:///auth/callback Valid post logout redirect URIs https:/// Web origins empty Under Advanced > Advanced settings set Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method to S256.
Copy the secret from Credentials into a Kubernetes Secret in the instance namespace:
kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-oidc \ --from-literal=client-secret=''
data.2-create-the-role-and-map-it-into-the-to:
Clients > dark-factory > Roles > Create role: name board-member. Assign it to the users (or a group) who may operate the factory.
Clients > dark-factory > Client scopes > dark-factory-dedicated > Configure a new mapper > User Client Role:
Setting Value Name roles Client ID dark-factory Multivalued On Token Claim Name roles (auth.rolesClaim) Claim JSON Type String Add to ID token On Add to access token optional The default resource_access.dark-factory.roles claim is nested and is not read. The claim must be a top-level list, for example "roles": ["board-member"].
A role removed in Keycloak takes effect when the access token expires (default 5 minutes) and is refreshed.
Revoke Refresh Token (refresh token rotation) is supported: the control plane refreshes each session once, even when several requests arrive with an expired token at the same time.
data.3-configure-the-control-plane#3. Configu:
Helm values (all settings: Control plane settings):
oidc: issuerUrl: https://id.example.org/realms/dark-factory clientId: dark-factory existingSecret: dark-factory-oidc clientSecretKey: client-secret publicUrl: https://factory.example.org rolesClaim: roles Then check the login as in Verify.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause Invalid parameter: redirect_uri at Keycloak The redirect URI does not match auth.publicUrl + /auth/callback. 403 for a user who has the role The mapper does not add the claim to the ID token, or auth.rolesClaim differs from Token Claim Name. Login unavailable (502) The control plane cannot reach auth.issuerUrl; check the NetworkPolicy and the issuer URL. Login failed (400) The login state does not match, e.g. the login page was opened in another browser or the cookie was blocked. Logged out every few minutes The refresh was refused: the Keycloak SSO session or refresh token expired, or the client lost Standard flow.

data:
An instance keeps all its state in one PostgreSQL database (version 17, the version the tests run against). Dark Factory separates the privileges between two roles:
Role Helm value (default) Used by Rights Owner database.owner.user (dark_factory_owner) only the migrate job (pre-install and pre-upgrade hook) owns the database and the schema database.schema (dark_factory), runs the migrations, grants the application role its rights Application database.app.user (dark_factory_app) dark-factory serve SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on the tables, USAGE, SELECT on sequences, append-only (SELECT, INSERT) on audit_log; no DDL Each password lives in a Secret in the instance namespace:
Secret (Helm value, default) Key Mounted into database.owner.existingSecret (dark-factory-db-owner) password (database.owner.passwordKey) the migrate job database.app.existingSecret (dark-factory-db-app) password (database.app.passwordKey) the control plane; also the migrate job when it manages the application role kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-db-owner --from-literal=password='' kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-db-app --from-literal=password=''
data.connection-settings#Connection settings: database: host: postgres.databases.svc port: 5432 database: dark_factory schema: dark_factory maxConnections: 16 # pool size of the control plane All database values: chart README.
data.option-a-the-migration-job-manages-the-a:
Only the owner exists beforehand, and it needs CREATEROLE:
CREATE ROLE dark_factory_owner LOGIN PASSWORD '' CREATEROLE; CREATE DATABASE dark_factory OWNER dark_factory_owner; On every install and upgrade the migrate job creates the application role (or sets its password from the Secret, which rotates it) and applies the grants. Helm values: none, database.migrate.manageAppRole is true by default.
data.option-b-both-roles-provisioned-outside-:
For declarative setups (CloudNativePG managed roles, Crossplane, Terraform, a DBA) where the owner must not have CREATEROLE. Create both roles as plain LOGIN roles:
CREATE ROLE dark_factory_owner LOGIN PASSWORD ''; CREATE ROLE dark_factory_app LOGIN PASSWORD ''; CREATE DATABASE dark_factory OWNER dark_factory_owner; \connect dark_factory CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS dark_factory AUTHORIZATION dark_factory_owner; Instead of owning the database, the owner may hold CREATE and CONNECT (with GRANT OPTION on CONNECT) on it. Then disable role management:
database: migrate: manageAppRole: false The migrate job still re-applies all grants to the existing application role on every install and upgrade; it only stops creating the role and setting its password.

data:
This guide installs one Dark Factory instance into a Kubernetes cluster with the Helm chart of a release. It ends with a working login. Dark Factory is pre-MVP: pin the chart version and read the release notes before you upgrade.
flowchart LR A[Prerequisites] --> B[PostgreSQL roles] B --> C[OIDC client] C --> D[Secrets] D --> E[helm install] E --> F[First login]
data.1-create-the-postgresql-roles#1. Create:
Dark Factory uses two roles: an owner that runs the migrations and an application role that serves requests (no DDL rights). The simplest setup lets the migration job manage the application role. Then only the owner needs to exist, and it needs CREATEROLE:
CREATE ROLE dark_factory_owner LOGIN PASSWORD '' CREATEROLE; CREATE DATABASE dark_factory OWNER dark_factory_owner; Put both passwords into Secrets in the instance namespace (the application password is set on the role by the migration job):
kubectl create namespace dark-factory kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-db-owner --from-literal=password='' kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-db-app --from-literal=password='' If you provision roles declaratively and the owner must not have CREATEROLE, create both roles yourself: see Database.
data.2-create-the-oidc-client#2. Create the O:
Create the confidential client dark-factory and the role board-member, and map the role into a top-level roles claim of the ID token. The steps are in Keycloak (with Dex: Dex). At the end you have a client secret; store it:
kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic dark-factory-oidc --from-literal=client-secret=''
data.3-write-the-helm-values#3. Write the Hel:
values.yaml for a cluster with Kata Containers, an external PostgreSQL and Keycloak:
database: host: postgres.databases.svc database: dark_factory oidc: issuerUrl: https://id.example.org/realms/dark-factory publicUrl: https://factory.example.org sandboxNamespace: runtimeClassName: kata # Publish the UI through an existing Gateway API Gateway. httpRoute: enabled: true parentRefs: - name: public namespace: gateway-system hostnames: - factory.example.org networkPolicy: ingressController: namespaceSelector: kubernetes.io/metadata.name: gateway-system Everything else has a default; the chart README lists every key. Set oidc.publicUrl to the URL the browser uses: without it the web UI stays unavailable.
data.4-install#4. Install:
Pin the version. Releases are named YYYY.M.N (for example 2026.11.0); the list is on the GitHub releases page.
helm install dark-factory oci://ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/charts/dark-factory \ --namespace dark-factory \ --version 2026.11.0 \ --values values.yaml The chart runs the migrate job first (pre-install hook), then starts the control plane and the gateway. Check that both are ready:
kubectl -n dark-factory get pods kubectl -n dark-factory rollout status deploy/dark-factory-control-plane The images default to the chart’s appVersion, so the images match the chart version.
data.5-first-login#5. First login: Give your Keycloak user the client role board-member. Open the oidc.publicUrl. You are redirected to Keycloak and, after the login, to the task list. The profile menu (your initials) shows the version of the running instance and links to the docs of exactly that version. A user without the role gets 403; other symptoms are in the Keycloak troubleshooting table.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Using Dark Factory: credentials, projects and personas, then the first task. Forges: connect your Forgejo or GitHub repositories. Security: what the sandbox can and cannot do. Observability: log format and levels, metrics and traces.
data.prerequisites#Prerequisites: What Why Kubernetes 1.36 or newer The runtime and the harness reach sandboxes as image volumes (kubeVersion of the chart). Kata Containers with a RuntimeClass (this guide: kata) Sandboxes run untrusted agent code and should run in a microVM. Without it they run in the cluster’s default runtime. cert-manager (with the CSI driver) Issues the mTLS certificates of the control plane, the gateway and every sandbox. A CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (Cilium or any other) Sandboxes may only reach the gateway; the chart ships a default-deny policy. PostgreSQL 17, reachable from the cluster The only state of an instance (the version the tests run against). An OIDC provider: Keycloak (this guide) or Dex Login to the web UI. A Gateway API Gateway (or any other way to publish port 8080 of the control plane) with a TLS certificate The browser needs an HTTPS URL; it is also the OIDC redirect target. helm 3.8 or newer and access to ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory The chart is an OCI artifact.
data.upgrade#Upgrade: Run helm upgrade with the new --version and the same values. The migration job runs again before the new control plane starts. Read the release notes first.

data:
Dark Factory talks to external systems through plugins: WebAssembly components that run inside the control plane in a sandbox (Wasmtime). A plugin sees no credentials; the control plane adds them to each request and limits the plugin to the hosts of its route.
Forges: Forgejo and GitHub, for pull requests, issues and review feedback.

A forge plugin opens and updates the draft pull request of a task, comments on issues and reads review feedback. Agents never call the forge API: the control plane calls it with the project’s forge credential. Git clone and push go through the gateway’s Git proxy.
Forge Plugin Default route Forgejo forgejo every host no other plugin claims (default plugin) GitHub, GitHub Enterprise Server github github.com How a project’s repository host selects a plugin, the instance configuration keys and the GitHub how-tos: Plugin configuration.
data.connect-a-repository#Connect a repositor:
Create a token for a bot account with write access to the repository:
Forgejo: scopes write:repository, write:issue and read:user; the review loop needs repository admin (token scopes). GitHub: a fine-grained token with Pull requests, Issues and Contents read/write and Metadata read (connect a GitHub repository). Store it in a Secret in the instance namespace:
kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic forge-token --from-file=token= In the web UI, Credentials → New credential reference: a name, Secret forge-token, key token. The control plane stores only the reference, never the token.
Projects → New project: the repository URL (https://git.example.org//.git) and that credential as forge credential. The hint below the URL names the plugin that serves it.
data.plugin-images#Plugin images:
Each plugin ships as its own image (FROM scratch, one file /plugin.wasm). The kubelet pulls it and the control plane pod mounts it read-only as an image volume at /plugins/. The images follow the chart version (appVersion) unless pinned:
plugins: forgejo: image: digest: sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef Upgrade a plugin: set the new plugins..image.tag (or digest) and run helm upgrade. The control plane rolls; a plugin image that cannot be pulled keeps the new pod in ContainerCreating while the old pods keep serving.
Cluster without image volumes: build a control plane image that contains the component and set a path instead of an image:
FROM ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/control-plane:2026.11.0 COPY plugin.wasm /custom/forgejo.wasm image: controlPlane: repository: registry.example.org/control-plane-with-plugin plugins: forgejo: image: null path: /custom/forgejo.wasm Instance without GitHub: plugins.github: null removes the entry; projects on github.com then go to the default plugin.
All plugin values: chart README.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause The control plane pod does not start; kubectl describe pod shows a failed pull of the volume plugin- The plugin image or tag does not exist, the registry needs credentials (image.pullSecrets apply to plugin images too), or the cluster has no image volume support. A project fails with a config error naming a plugin That plugin did not load (log event “forge plugin not loaded” with the reason). Its projects never fall back to another plugin. serve stops at startup A host claimed by two plugins, two plugins without hosts, an apiUrl without https://, or no forge plugin loaded at all (Startup). Pull request comments fail with unauthorized (Forgejo) The bot account is not repository admin, which the review loop needs.

data:
Section plugins of the instance configuration (/etc/dark-factory/config.yaml) is a map from plugin name to its settings. The host does not know plugin-specific keys; settings is passed through to the plugin as wasi:config/store. hosts and authScheme are host-side keys: the host enforces them, the plugin never sees them.
plugins: forgejo: path: /plugins/forgejo/plugin.wasm callTimeoutSeconds: 30 memoryMib: 64 settings: wip-prefixes: "WIP:,[WIP]" # no hosts: default plugin github: path: /plugins/github/plugin.wasm authScheme: bearer hosts: - host: github.com apiUrl: https://api.github.com - host: ghe.example.org apiUrl: https://ghe.example.org/api/v3 Key Required Default Effect plugins..path yes none Component file. plugins..callTimeoutSeconds no 30 Upper bound of one plugin call (retries excluded). Guest code is stopped by epoch interruption (50 ms granularity), network waits by a timeout. A timed-out call fails with internal; the instance is discarded. plugins..memoryMib no 64 Linear memory limit per instance. Exceeding it fails the call with internal. plugins..hosts no [] Repository hosts this plugin serves. Each entry is a string host[:port] or a map {host, apiUrl}; the map rejects unknown keys. Hosts are DNS names, IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 addresses; they are lowercased, a trailing dot and port 443 are dropped, any other port stays part of the host. A host may be claimed by one entry only. An entry without hosts (or with []) is the default plugin; at most one is allowed. plugins..hosts[].apiUrl no https:// API base URL for this host. Must start with https:// and have no userinfo, query or fragment; host lowercased, port 443 and a trailing / dropped, the path is kept (https://ghe.example.org/api/v3). Becomes the plugin’s base-url and the only authority its requests may reach. Only valid in the {host, apiUrl} form, which rejects unknown keys. plugins..authScheme no token How the project’s forge credential is sent: token → Authorization: token , bearer → Authorization: Bearer . The host sets the header on every request and replaces one set by the plugin. Applies to all hosts of the entry, the default plugin included. plugins..settings no {} String map handed to the plugin unchanged. The host adds base-url (the route’s apiUrl; for the default plugin scheme and authority of the project’s repo_url) and it wins over a configured one. Keys are documented by the plugin (Forgejo: wip-prefixes, see plugins/forgejo/README.md; GitHub: draft-mode, wip-prefixes, api-version, see plugins/github/README.md). Unknown keys fail parsing the configuration. An unknown authScheme value fails startup naming the plugin and the value (see “Startup”).
The Helm chart renders the section from its plugins.* values and mounts each plugin image (//deploy:plugin_forgejo_image, one file /plugin.wasm) as an image volume at /plugins/ (deploy/helm/dark-factory/README.md, “Plugins”). All plugins share one Wasmtime engine and epoch clock.
data.add-a-second-forge#Add a second forge:
Make the component available to the control plane (for the chart: a plugin image mounted at /plugins/).
Add an entry with the hosts it serves, the apiUrl where the API is not at https://, and the authScheme the forge expects. Give the existing entry hosts as well, so neither is a catch-all:
plugins: forgejo: path: /plugins/forgejo/plugin.wasm hosts: [git.example.org] github: path: /plugins/github/plugin.wasm authScheme: bearer hosts: - host: github.com apiUrl: https://api.github.com Restart serve and check the “forge route” events: each host with the expected plugin and available=true.
Create projects with a repo_url on the new host and a forge credential for that forge.
data.add-github-enterprise-server#Add GitHub:
Add the host with its API URL. Settings apply to every host of an entry. A server older than the default API version 2026-03-10 needs api-version: "2022-11-28"; in the github entry that setting would also apply to github.com, so give the server its own entry with the same component:
plugins: github: path: /plugins/github/plugin.wasm authScheme: bearer hosts: - host: github.com apiUrl: https://api.github.com github-enterprise: path: /plugins/github/plugin.wasm authScheme: bearer hosts: - host: ghe.example.org apiUrl: https://ghe.example.org/api/v3 settings: api-version: "2022-11-28" Otherwise add {host: ghe.example.org, apiUrl: https://ghe.example.org/api/v3} to the github entry’s hosts. GraphQL goes to https://ghe.example.org/api/graphql without further configuration.
Restart serve and check the “forge route” event for ghe.example.org.
Connect repositories as above, with a token from the server, repository URLs https://ghe.example.org//.git and an egress rule for ghe.example.org. With a separate entry, the web UI shows these projects with the generic Git icon and the hint names that entry (“Served by the github-enterprise integration; …”).
data.connect-a-github-repository#Connect a Gi:
Check the route: the startup event “forge route” for github.com shows plugin=github and available=true. Without it, add the entry (see “Add a second forge”):
plugins: github: path: /plugins/github/plugin.wasm authScheme: bearer hosts: - host: github.com apiUrl: https://api.github.com Create a fine-grained personal access token for an account with write access, restricted to the project’s repositories (“Only select repositories”), with the repository permissions Pull requests read/write, Issues read/write, Contents read/write (Git clone and push) and Metadata read. A classic token needs repo. list-feedback reads each reviewer’s repository permission (GET .../collaborators/{username}/permission), which needs the account’s write access.
Store it in a Secret in the instance namespace (sandbox.instanceNamespace), for example kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic github-token --from-file=token=.
Credentials → “New credential reference”: a name, Secret name github-token, key token.
Projects → “New project”: repository URL https://github.com//.git and that credential as forge credential. The hint below the repository URL reads “Served by the GitHub integration; pull requests and issues use it.”
No egress rule for github.com is needed. The sandbox clones and pushes through the gateway’s Git proxy, which sends agent.gitUsername and the token upstream; API calls come from the control plane.
data.forge-routing#Forge routing:
Each forge call is routed by the host of the project’s repo_url, normalized like hosts (lowercase, port 443 dropped). Matching is exact: www.example.org, example.org and example.org:3000 are three hosts. A claimed host goes to the plugin claiming it, any other host to the default plugin. A plugin that did not load keeps its hosts: its projects get a config error naming the plugin and never fall through to the default, because their credential is meant for that forge.
flowchart TD H["host of repo_url (normalized)"] --> C{"listed in hosts?"} C -- yes --> CL{"claiming plugin loaded?"} CL -- yes --> R1["claiming plugin, base-url = apiUrl"] CL -- no --> E1["config error: plugin did not load"] C -- no --> D{"default plugin configured?"} D -- no --> E2["config error: no forge plugin serves host"] D -- yes --> DL{"default plugin loaded?"} DL -- yes --> R2["default plugin, base-url = scheme://authority of repo_url"] DL -- no --> E1 With more than one plugin, give every entry hosts: a default plugin also receives projects of forges nobody configured (for example gitlab.com sent to Forgejo) and fails with upstream 401/404. Without a default such projects get a clear config error.
data.forgejo-token-scopes#Forgejo token scope:
The bot account’s token needs write:repository (create and update pull requests, read branches), write:issue (comments on issues and pull requests) and read:user (list-feedback reads the token’s own account to label its comments bot; Forgejo 15 answers 403 without this scope). Read-only use needs read:repository, read:issue and read:user.
The account needs write access to the repository for pull requests and comments. The review loop (list-feedback) needs repository admin: it reads each author’s permission, which Forgejo only answers for site or repository admins. With write access only, list-feedback fails with unauthorized.
data.github#GitHub: The github plugin serves github.com and GitHub Enterprise Server. Its settings, draft modes and error mapping: plugins/github/README.md. The Helm chart’s default values route github.com to it.
data.startup#Startup:
Without a plugins section (or with an empty one) serve uses one entry forgejo with path /plugins/forgejo/plugin.wasm as the default plugin. As soon as plugins has an entry, there is no implicit forgejo. serve builds the routing table from the configuration alone. A configuration error stops startup before any plugin loads (event “control plane server failed”, field error): invalid `plugins` configuration: with one of host `` is claimed by plugins `` and `` plugins ``, `` have no `hosts`; at most one default plugin is allowed plugin ``: apiUrl `` must use https:// plugin ``: invalid apiUrl (not a URL, or with userinfo, query or fragment; the value is not echoed) plugin ``: invalid host in `hosts[]` (index from 0; the value is not echoed) plugin ``: unknown authScheme `` (use `token` or `bearer`) It loads every entry. An entry that fails (component missing or invalid, memoryMib too large, or no pull-requests export: “is not a forge plugin”) is logged at error (“forge plugin not loaded”, fields plugin, path, error) and stays in the table as unavailable. If no forge plugin loaded, serve exits with no forge plugin loaded: . Otherwise it logs the table at info: one “forge route” per claimed host (fields host, plugin, available, ordered by host), then “default forge route” (plugin, available) or “no default forge route”. Each successful load is logged at info (“plugin loaded”) with the fields plugin (name under plugins), path, bytes (component size) and compile_ms (load time: everything after the file read, i.e. import validation, compilation and pre-instantiation; the shared engine is created once before). Use it to see what the plugin costs at startup.
Plugin stderr is logged at info with the fields plugin (the name under plugins) and line; lines longer than 4 KiB are split.
Per project (database): repo_url (https:////[.git], without userinfo, query or fragment) selects the route and gives the repository; base-url comes from the route (see settings). forge_credential_id references the Kubernetes Secret holding the token. Secrets are read per call and not cached.
data.swap-a-plugin-for-a-host#Swap a plugin f:
Projects store no plugin name, so moving a host needs no data change.
Add the new entry (or change path of the existing one to replace only the component).
Move the host from the old entry’s hosts to the new one. Listing it in both fails startup with host `` is claimed by plugins ….
plugins: forgejo: path: /plugins/forgejo/plugin.wasm hosts: [git.example.org] forgejo-next: path: /plugins/forgejo-next/plugin.wasm hosts: [code.example.org] # moved from `forgejo` Check that the projects’ credentials fit the new plugin’s authScheme.
Restart serve; the “forge route” event for the host shows the new plugin. To roll back, move the host back.
data.troubleshoot-an-unroutable-project#Troub:
Read the error of the failed forge call (plugin configuration error: …):
no forge plugin serves host `` : no entry claims the host and there is no default plugin, or the host is not valid. Compare the host with the “forge route” events (port and www. count) and add it to the right entry’s hosts. forge plugin `` serving host `` did not load: find the startup event “forge plugin not loaded” with that plugin; its path and error name the cause. Fix it and restart. invalid repository URL: repo_url is not https:////[.git], or it has userinfo, a query or a fragment. The URL is not echoed: it may carry credentials. repository URL for host `` is not HTTPS: repo_url uses http://; use https://. the project has no forge credential: set the project’s forge credential. Open the project’s edit form. The hint below the repository URL names the routing result:
“Served by the integration; pull requests and issues use it.” “The integration claims this host but is not loaded: …” “The default integration is not loaded: …” “No forge integration applies: …” The project list shows the generic Git icon for a project no loaded integration serves (and for a project without a forge credential).
An upstream 401 or 404 instead of a config error usually means the project went to the default plugin. Check the “forge route” and “default forge route” events and add the host to the entry of its forge.
data.use-title-prefix-drafts#Use title-prefix:
The default draft-mode: native creates GitHub’s native draft pull requests, which also exist in private repositories on GitHub Free.
Pick the mode. Use title-prefix when a repository or GitHub Enterprise Server instance rejects native drafts (creating a draft fails with invalid-input naming draft-mode: title-prefix), or for a WIP: marker in the title consistent with Forgejo. auto creates native drafts where possible and falls back to the title prefix elsewhere, at the cost of one failed request per draft and a warning (event “plugin stderr”, plugin=github, level info).
Set it in the entry’s settings (chart: plugins.github.settings):
plugins: github: # path, authScheme, hosts unchanged settings: draft-mode: title-prefix # or auto Restart serve. Open drafts keep working: reading recognizes the title prefix and the native flag.

data: Logging: log format and levels of all components, and the sandbox session events. Telemetry: OpenTelemetry metrics and traces of the control plane and the gateway.

All components (control plane serve, migrate, gateway, and the sandbox runtime factory-agent run) share the same two settings.
Variable Required Default Effect DF_LOG_FORMAT no text text: human-readable lines. json: one JSON object per line with timestamp, level, target and fields (fields.message is the message). Also available as --log-format. An unknown value makes the process exit with an error naming the variable. RUST_LOG no info Log level in EnvFilter syntax (info, debug, info,df_web=debug). Unset, empty or invalid values log at info; an invalid value also logs a warning naming RUST_LOG. Clap usage errors are printed to stderr as plain text in both formats.
data.per-component-levels#Per-component level: Component Level source Control plane, migrate RUST_LOG (Helm: controlPlane.logLevel) Gateway RUST_LOG (Helm: gateway.logLevel) Sandbox runtime instance config sandbox.logLevel (default info), set by the control plane as the sandbox’s RUST_LOG The control plane sets DF_LOG_FORMAT in every sandbox to its own effective format. Helm values: logging.format (all components), see deploy/helm/dark-factory/README.md.
data.sandbox-session-events#Sandbox session e:
factory-agent logs the session at INFO so a run can be followed from the pod log: run assigned, harness started, harness session ready, prompt received, turn started, user message delivered, tool call (title, kind, origin, input), tool call status changed, plan updated, turn ended, notices (WARN for warning and error notices), push reports and the run report.
input is the tool’s raw input cut to 512 bytes (input_truncated=true when cut). Operators who cannot accept tool input in logs set sandbox.logLevel: warn. Agent message and thought chunks are logged at DEBUG only. Tool output, tool content, prompt content and credentials are never logged.

data:
The control plane (dark-factory serve) and the gateway (dark-factory gateway) export OpenTelemetry metrics and, optionally, traces. migrate and the sandbox runtime export nothing: the runtime sends its measurements to the control plane over the agent channel (RuntimeTiming), and the control plane derives the run metrics from the messages it persists.
flowchart LR runtime[Sandbox runtime] -- "agent messages incl. RuntimeTiming (mTLS, durable outbox)" --> cp[Control plane] cp -- "after commit" --> meters[OTel meter provider] gw[Gateway] --> meters meters -- "GET /metrics :9464" --> prom[Prometheus] meters -- "OTLP/gRPC push" --> coll[OTel Collector]
data.configuration#Configuration:
Standard OTEL_* variables; Helm renders them from telemetry.* (see deploy/helm/dark-factory/README.md).
Variable Required Default Effect OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER no prometheus Comma-separated list of prometheus, otlp, none. none alone disables metrics. An unknown value stops the process at startup, the error names the variable. OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST no 0.0.0.0 Address of the scrape endpoint. OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_PORT no 9464 Port of GET /metrics, separate from all other listeners. OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER no none otlp exports spans; none installs no exporter and opens no connection. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG no parentbased_always_on always_on, always_off, traceidratio (argument: ratio from 0 to 1, default 1), each also with the prefix parentbased_. Other values stop the process at startup. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _HEADERS, _INSECURE, _TIMEOUT with otlp none OTLP over gRPC. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL (also _METRICS_PROTOCOL, _TRACES_PROTOCOL) accepts only grpc; any other value stops the process at startup. An endpoint without scheme uses https; the native root store and a mounted private CA are honoured. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL no 60000 (ms) Push interval of the otlp metrics exporter. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME no dark-factory-control-plane / dark-factory-gateway service.name. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES no none Extra resource attributes. Every metric and span carries the resource attributes service.name, service.version and service.instance.id (pod name, else host name). service.version is the release version the binary was built with, dev for unstamped builds. Build-time variable DF_VERSION (optional, default dev; an empty value also gives dev): Bazel sets it from --//build:version=, plain cargo with DF_VERSION= cargo build. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.version=… overrides it.
Export failures never affect the component; the SDK logs them at ERROR once per export interval. On shutdown pending exports are flushed within the shutdown grace period (30 s) counted from the signal: what the listeners did not use is left for the flush.
data.control-plane#Control plane:
Instrument Type Unit Attributes Source df.runs.ended counter project, outcome RunReport df.run.duration histogram s project, outcome run start to RunReport df.agent.turns counter project, stop_reason TurnEnded df.agent.tokens counter project, model, token_type (input, output, cache_read, cache_write) TurnEnded.usage df.agent.tool_calls counter project, kind, origin, status (completed, failed) terminal status of a tool call df.agent.pushes counter project, target, status PushReport df.agent.runtime.duration histogram s project, operation, result (ok, error) RuntimeTiming df.agent.runtime.rejected counter project, operation RuntimeTiming with a duration of zero or more than 7 days df.agent.connections up-down counter project open agent channel streams df.agent.reconnects counter project streams of runs that had one before operation is one of workspace_prepare, harness_start, turn, push, finalize. outcome, stop_reason, kind, origin, target and status are the lower-case protobuf enum names without prefix (end_turn, task_branch); unknown numbers are unspecified.
Attributes that originate from the sandbox are bounded: model is cut to 64 bytes and after 32 distinct values per process further ones are other. Run ids, task keys, tool titles, repository URLs and hosts are never attributes.
data.gateway#Gateway: Instrument Type Unit Attributes Meaning df.gateway.connections counter decision (allowed, denied), reason (deny reason or none) proxy requests by final decision, counted when they end df.gateway.active_connections up-down counter requests connected to their destination df.gateway.bytes counter By direction (upstream: sandbox to destination, downstream) relayed bytes df.gateway.policy_version gauge version of the last applied allowlist snapshot
data.how-to-enable-tracing#How to enable trac:
Run an OTLP/gRPC collector that Jaeger, Tempo or similar reads from.
Set the endpoint and enable traces, in Helm:
telemetry: traces: enabled: true sampler: parentbased_traceidratio samplerArg: '0.1' otlp: endpoint: https://otel-collector.observability.svc:4317 or as variables: OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=....
Look for service.name dark-factory-control-plane and dark-factory-gateway.
Spans pass the same RUST_LOG filter as log events: RUST_LOG=info exports the INFO spans listed above.
data.instruments#Instruments: Recording is best-effort: the control plane records after the transaction that persists a message committed, never for replayed messages, so a crash between commit and recording loses the sample. Run instruments carry project (project key). Prometheus renders df.agent.turns as df_agent_turns_total and appends the unit (df_run_duration_seconds).
data.spans#Spans:
Only with OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp. Attributes never contain credentials, prompts or tool input/output.
Span Attributes http.request http.request.method, http.route, http.response.status_code (UI and gateway health listeners; the /metrics scrape endpoint gets no span) agent.session run_id agent.persist_batch messages (count) gateway.connect method, decision, host (allowed requests only) Spans of the runtime and trace context propagation over the agent channel are not part of this.

data: Upgrades: moving to a new release and what cannot be rolled back. Backup and restore: what holds state and how to save it. Troubleshooting: runs that do not start or end unexpectedly.

All state of an instance is in its PostgreSQL database: projects, personas, credential references, tasks, runs, transcripts (binary content included), requests, egress rules, push records and the audit log. Back up the database; everything else can be recreated.
What Where Back up? Database PostgreSQL, schema dark_factory yes Code the forge: task branches factory/task/ and WIP snapshots factory/wip/ by the forge’s own backup Secret values (forge and harness tokens, database passwords, OIDC client secret) Kubernetes Secrets in the instance namespace yes, with your usual Secret handling; the database only holds references Task volumes PVCs in the sandbox namespace no: a cache; the next run re-clones from the task branch and the WIP snapshot Live traffic events gateway memory no: ephemeral by design Helm values your values.yaml keep it in version control
data.back-up#Back up:
Any PostgreSQL backup method works (pg_dump, your operator’s scheduled backups, volume snapshots of the database server). A logical dump of the instance’s database:
pg_dump --format=custom --file=dark-factory-$(date +%F).dump \ "postgresql://dark_factory_owner@postgres.databases.svc/dark_factory" Take one before every upgrade: schema migrations cannot be undone (Upgrades).
data.restore#Restore: Scale the control plane to zero, so nothing writes during the restore: kubectl -n dark-factory scale deploy/dark-factory-control-plane --replicas=0. Restore into an empty database owned by the owner role, for example pg_restore --no-owner --role=dark_factory_owner --dbname=dark_factory dark-factory-2026-11-04.dump. Run helm upgrade with the release that matches the backup. The migrate job re-applies the application role’s grants. Scale the control plane back up. Runs that were active when the backup was taken have no sandbox anymore; they end as sandbox_lost and their tasks are queued again.

data: The task’s details show the outcome of each run; the control plane log has the reason (see Logging).
data.a-run-cannot-do-its-work#A run cannot do: Symptom Cause and fix A network-access request for a host The host has no allow rule: approve the request or add a rule (Network access). Git clone or push fails with 403 The gateway does not know the pod yet (retried), or the path names another task. Git fails with 502 The forge rejected the project’s forge credential: check the token and its scopes (Forges). git push prints df:… A push check rejected it; in approval mode a push-check-exception request appears in the inbox (Git proxy). The task becomes rate_limited The model provider’s usage limit; the task resumes at the shown time. No pull request appears The task branch has no commit ahead of the base branch yet, or the forge plugin failed (retried at every push and at run end; see the control plane log).
data.a-task-does-not-start#A task does not st: Symptom Cause and fix The task stays queued All run slots are busy (runs.maxConcurrent, default 4), or its resume time lies ahead (shown in the details). The run ends provisioning_failed The sandbox pod or the task volume could not be created: check the events in the sandbox namespace (kubectl -n dark-factory-sandboxes get events), the ResourceQuota, the storage class and the project’s sandbox image. The task is retried automatically up to 3 times. The run ends connect_timeout The pod started but the runtime did not reach the control plane within runs.connectTimeoutSeconds (600 s): check the pod log, the certificate from cert-manager’s CSI driver, and the NetworkPolicy from the sandbox namespace to the control plane’s agent port. The run ends sandbox_lost The pod disappeared: deleted, evicted, out of memory, or the image could not be pulled. Retried automatically. The run fails right after connecting The persona’s harness credential is missing: check the credential reference and the Secret.
data.login-problems#Login problems: See the troubleshooting tables of Keycloak and Dex.

data: Dark Factory is pre-MVP: any release may change the configuration, the database schema or the web UI incompatibly, and there are no migration guarantees between releases yet. Read the release notes on the releases page before every upgrade.
data.release-specific-steps#Release-specific: Some releases need a step beyond helm upgrade, for example removing the forge host from the egress rules after the switch to the Git proxy. They are listed in the release notes and in the chart README.
data.rolling-back#Rolling back: Schema migrations only go forward: there are no down migrations. helm rollback restores the old images and values but not the old schema, and an older control plane may not start on a newer schema. To go back, restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back the release.
data.upgrade-a-release#Upgrade a release:
Back up the database (Backup and restore).
Let active runs finish, or accept that they are cut off: a run whose sandbox disappears ends with sandbox_lost and its task is queued again automatically.
Upgrade with the new chart version and your values:
helm upgrade dark-factory oci://ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/charts/dark-factory \ --namespace dark-factory \ --version 2026.11.1 \ --values values.yaml The migrate job runs first (pre-upgrade hook) and applies the new schema migrations; then the control plane and the gateway roll. Check:
kubectl -n dark-factory get pods kubectl -n dark-factory rollout status deploy/dark-factory-control-plane The profile menu shows the new version and links to its docs.
The control plane, runtime, gateway and plugin images follow the chart’s appVersion unless you pinned them; a pinned plugin image keeps its version until you change it.

data:
Configuration references of the components:
Sandbox runtime: environment variables of factory-agent run. Agent channel: the connection between the sandbox runtime and the control plane. Plugins: forge plugins, their routing and settings.
dark-factory serve starts the agent port and the run scheduler. Settings come from the instance configuration file (--config, default /etc/dark-factory/config.yaml).
data.configuration#Configuration:
Key Required Default Effect server.agentPort no 9443 Port of the mTLS agent service, separate from server.httpPort. agent.tls.certFile yes none PEM server certificate (chain) of the agent port. serve refuses to start without agent.tls. The three files are checked for changes at most every 10 s; changed (rotated) material applies to new connections without a restart, material that does not parse is ignored with a warning. agent.tls.keyFile yes none PEM private key of certFile. agent.tls.clientCaFile yes none PEM CA bundle. Client certificates must chain to it. agent.commitIdentity.name / .email no Dark Factory / dark-factory@localhost Commit identity in Assign.workspace.commit_identity. agent.gitUsername no dark-factory User name the gateway’s Git proxy sends with the project’s forge token. harness.claudeCode.image no ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/claude-harness:0.95.0 Harness image, mounted read-only at /opt/harness/claude-code in the sandbox of every run whose project has no adapter command. The tag is the adapter version. The chart renders it from image.harness.claudeCode.*. harness.claudeCode.adapterCommand no ["/opt/harness/claude-code/bin/claude-agent-acp"] ACP adapter command from the harness image; a project’s own adapter command replaces it (and the harness image mount). Personas have no adapter command. harness.claudeCode.env no {} Non-secret environment for the harness (Assign.harness.acp.env). harness.claudeCode.settingsJson no "" Claude Code settings.json content, written by the runtime before every start. runs.maxWallClockSeconds no 7200 Assign.budgets.max_wall_clock. Counts from the runtime’s first Hello, not from run creation. A value too large to represent as a date means no limit. runs.connectTimeoutSeconds no 600 Time from run creation until the runtime opens its stream; then the run fails with connect_timeout. runs.cancelGraceSeconds no 300 Grace after the wall-clock budget. runs.keepAliveSeconds no 600 How long a run waits for a follow-up after a normal turn end (awaiting_input) before the control plane sends Release and the run ends end_turn. 0 releases right after the turn. Idle time counts toward maxWallClockSeconds. volumes.retainAfterCloseSeconds no 604800 (7 days) The volume of a completed or cancelled task without an active run is deleted this long after its last run ended. The check runs once per hour on the replica holding the instance Lease (not without a cluster). 0 deletes at the next check; a value too large to represent as a date means never. volumes.idleTtlSeconds no 2592000 (30 days) The volume of any task without an active run is deleted this long after its last run ended; same check and value rules as retainAfterCloseSeconds. The next run creates a fresh volume, clones again and restores the WIP snapshot. A board member can delete a volume at once with “Reset workspace” (crates/df-web/README.md). runs.maxConcurrent no 4 At least 1 (0 is rejected at startup). Runs that may be non-terminal at the same time, counted across all replicas. Further due tasks keep their status until a slot frees and then start oldest resume time first. runs.maxAutoResumes no 3 Consecutive automatic resumes after sandbox_lost, connect_timeout or provisioning_failed (backoff 2 min x (resumes + 1)); then the task becomes failed. A message or a run that ends with a RunReport resets the count; a capacity rejection does not count. web.showHiddenBlocks no false Show transcript content blocks marked hidden (instructions for the agent, e.g. the set_task_title request) in the task page and the queued message stack, muted and labeled “Instruction for the agent”. Hidden blocks are always delivered to the harness. Read at startup; a change needs a restart. The Helm chart sets agent.tls to the cert-manager secret mounted at /etc/dark-factory/tls.
The three files are checked for changes by the first connection that arrives at least 10 s after the last check; changed material applies to new connections without a restart, and material that does not parse is ignored (logged) until fixed. At most 256 TLS handshakes run at the same time.
data.database-changes#Database changes: 20261019000001_task_completion_summary.sql adds tasks.completion_summary (summary passed to complete_task, posted on the pull request when the run completes) and runs.connected_at (first Hello; start of the wall-clock budget).
data.human-stop-and-cancel#Human stop and can:
A board member stops the active run (POST /tasks/{key}/stop) or cancels the task (POST /tasks/{key}/cancel, which stops the run too). Both set runs.stop_requested_at.
A connected run in preparing, running or awaiting_input moves to finalizing; the session holding the stream sends Cancel, the runtime reports cancelled and the task becomes waiting. A run that is already finalizing is not marked by a stop (cancelling the task still marks it). A run without a connection (pending, provisioning, connecting) is ended cancelled by the scheduler on the next notification or tick and its sandbox is torn down. The task volume is kept. A stopped run that has not ended 120 s after the stop is torn down and ends cancelled with detail stop-timeout (volume kept). Task status cancelled is kept when the run ends. A message reopens the task (queued); the next run starts after the stopped run ended. Only messages queued after the stop requeue the task at run end; older undelivered messages leave it waiting. Cancelling discards the undelivered messages and closes the pending requests (task-cancelled). No pull request is opened or marked ready for a cancelled task; an existing one is left as it is.
data.idle-run-keep-alive#Idle run (keep-alive: After a normal turn end the runtime reports AWAITING_INPUT: the run becomes awaiting_input and the task waiting (it stays running while a message is undelivered). The replica holding the stream sends Release at the last persisted TurnEnded + runs.keepAliveSeconds; a replica that takes over, or a run that reconnects after the deadline, computes the same deadline. Before it sends Release (or Cancel for a task marked done) the control plane moves the run to finalizing; no prompt is sent to a finalizing run, a message queued meanwhile makes the task queued and the run end starts the next run. A message for an awaiting_input run sets the task running, starts no run and is forwarded at once.
data.protocol-behavior#Protocol behavior: Identity: the client certificate must carry the URI SAN spiffe://dark-factory/ns//pod//; SandboxProvider::resolve_identity maps SAN and peer IP to a run. Terminal runs are rejected with UNAUTHENTICATED. Handshake: Hello first (else FAILED_PRECONDITION), then HelloAck, HarnessCredentials, Assign, then the prompts: undelivered prompts that are already forwarded (task_messages.forwarded_at set) are sent again, held-back ones are claimed (marked forwarded) and sent only while no turn is open (no persisted TurnStarted without a later TurnEnded). After a persisted TurnEnded the held-back prompts are sent. See “Queued messages reach the runtime between turns” in contract/README.md. HarnessCredentials precede Assign because the runtime ignores credentials that arrive later. Timeouts: enforce_timeouts ends every overdue run it can; a run that fails to end (or whose row cannot be read) is logged and does not stop the others. Ordering and delivery: messages are persisted in batches of up to 50 per transaction, duplicates (seq <= runs.last_persisted_seq, blobs included) are dropped, a gap closes the stream with DATA_LOSS, and the cumulative ack is sent after commit. Effects of the messages before a gap (teardown, pull request) still run. A message with an unknown body keeps its sequence number and is ignored. Tool calls and credential requests that arrive after the run ended (for example after a hard stop) are refused: an error result and DeniedReason, nothing is executed or granted. Pull request work after a PushReport or RunReport runs beside the stream (60 s limit each), so a slow forge delays neither acks, Cancel nor prompts. If marking the pull request ready fails, the completion summary is still posted. Shutdown (SIGTERM): the scheduler lets provisioning in flight finish (10 s); sessions stop reading, finish their in-flight tool calls and credential requests (up to 20 s, then they are aborted) and end their streams; the listeners get 30 s before they are aborted. A runtime failing before Hello is logged and answered with its gRPC status. Limits: 16 MiB per message (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED above), HTTP/2 keepalive 30 s / 20 s, 10 s for the TLS handshake. Tool calls and credential requests run off the stream loop and are awaited (up to 60 s) when the stream ends. A tool call is claimed by call_id (tool_calls row) before it runs and executed at most once: a repeat gets the stored result, a call still running gets an error “in progress”, and a claim without a result after 5 minutes is closed with an error and never executed. The forge is called without an open database transaction. Executed calls are audited as tool_call.execute. Git credentials are granted only when protocol, host and path equal the project’s repository URL (a trailing .git is optional). Secret values are never logged or stored.
data.run-lifecycle#Run lifecycle:
stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> pending: task queued, no active run pending --> provisioning: volume ensured pending --> failed: provisioning_failed provisioning --> connecting: provider Started (pod IP) provisioning --> failed: provisioning_failed connecting --> preparing: Hello connecting --> failed: connect_timeout preparing --> running: PhaseChanged RUNNING running --> awaiting_input: PhaseChanged AWAITING_INPUT (turn ended) awaiting_input --> running: PhaseChanged RUNNING (follow-up prompt) awaiting_input --> finalizing: idle deadline (Release) or mark done (Cancel) running --> finalizing: PhaseChanged FINALIZING finalizing --> succeeded: RunReport completed / end_turn / limit_reached / rate_limited finalizing --> cancelled: RunReport cancelled finalizing --> failed: RunReport failed preparing --> failed: sandbox_lost running --> failed: sandbox_lost, hard stop preparing --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) running --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) awaiting_input --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) pending --> cancelled: human stop provisioning --> cancelled: human stop connecting --> cancelled: human stop finalizing --> cancelled: stop timeout (120 s) A RunReport is accepted in any non-terminal state. Cancel is sent by the replica holding the stream at connect + maxWallClock + cancelGrace (and at the handshake if that moment has passed). The scheduler tears the sandbox down at connect + maxWallClock + 2 x cancelGrace. Prompts and Cancel are not sent once the run has ended; the prompt stays queued for the next run.
Run outcome Run state Task status completed succeeded in_review end_turn succeeded waiting limit_reached succeeded limit_reached cancelled cancelled waiting (cancelled if a board member cancelled the task) blocked blocked waiting rate_limited succeeded rate_limited with a resume time (the retry time, or one hour ahead) failed failed failed provisioning_failed, connect_timeout, sandbox_lost failed queued with a resume time and the resume count + 1, until runs.maxAutoResumes, then failed provisioning_failed with detail capacity (quota exceeded) failed queued in 2 minutes, resume count unchanged If prompts are still undelivered when a run ends with an outcome other than failed-class or rate_limited, the task becomes queued and the next run starts with them. A task a board member marked done (completed) keeps its status when its run ends, unless prompts are undelivered.

data: factory-agent run reads its configuration from environment variables. The values are read once at startup (config.rs).
data.environment-variables#Environment variab: Variable Required Default Effect DF_CONTROL_PLANE_ADDR yes none Address of the control plane gRPC endpoint. host:port is accepted; https:// is prepended when no http:// or https:// scheme is given. DF_CONTROL_PLANE_SERVER_NAME yes none TLS server name checked against the control plane certificate. DF_TLS_DIR no /run/factory/tls Directory with ca.crt (instance CA), tls.crt and tls.key (pod identity). Re-read on every connection attempt, so rotated certificates are picked up on reconnect. Git trusts ca.crt only for the gateway’s Git proxy (http..sslCAInfo: -c on the clone, then .git/config); other hosts keep the system trust store. DF_DATA_DIR no /data Persistent volume. The runtime uses repo/ (workspace checkout), home/ (harness $HOME, session logs) and runtime/ (outbox segments, run.json). DF_RUN_DIR no /run/factory Ephemeral runtime directory. Holds runtime.sock and the wip.index scratch file. Also exported to the harness. DF_RUNTIME_SOCK no /run/factory/runtime.sock Path of the runtime Unix socket. Read by the mcp subcommand (also available as --socket), which the harness starts as a child process. run creates the socket at $DF_RUN_DIR/runtime.sock and exports that path to its children. DF_LOG_FORMAT no text Log format of run: text (human-readable) or json (one JSON object per line). Also available as --log-format. Any other value makes the process exit before it starts. The control plane sets it to its own format. RUST_LOG no info Log level in EnvFilter syntax, for example info or info,factory_agent=debug. Unset, empty or invalid values log at info; an invalid value also logs a warning naming RUST_LOG. The control plane sets it from sandbox.logLevel. DEBUG adds agent message and thought chunks. A missing required variable makes run log invalid configuration and exit with status 1.
data.fixed-settings#Fixed settings:
These are compiled in and not configurable.
Setting Value Effect Agent core.hooksPath /opt/factory/hooks-empty Read-only empty hooks directory from the image. Outbox size 256 MiB, segments of 16 MiB Soft cap: senders wait when it is full; a message already taken from the queue is still stored at shutdown. Wait for Assign 10 min run exits with status 1 when the control plane sends no Assign. Handshake steps 15 s each Connect, stream open and HelloAck; then backoff and retry. Final report flush window 10 min After finalize the runtime keeps reconnecting until every outbox message, the RunReport included, is acknowledged; then it exits. If the window passes, it exits with the messages left in the outbox and the control plane later ends the run sandbox_lost and resumes the task. The window does not extend the run’s wall-clock budget. Git commands 5 min each A clone, fetch or push that takes longer is killed and fails prepare or finalize. Git retries 3, after 1 s, 5 s and 15 s Clone, fetch and push that fail transiently are retried (see “Git retries” below). Factory tool call 30 min Wait for a ToolCallResult; then the tool call returns an error. Harness exit grace 5 s Time to exit after the ACP connection closed, then it is killed.
data.other-inputs#Other inputs: Input Source Effect HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY (and lowercase) environment Forwarded to git and the harness.
data.startup-and-shutdown-behavior#Startup an: Outbox. The outbox opens with the state stored in $DF_DATA_DIR/runtime/run.json. The run id in HelloAck or Assign decides whether that state is kept or discarded. Message order. HarnessCredentials must arrive before Assign. Credentials that arrive later are ignored and reported as a runtime.harness_credentials_late notice. A Cancel that arrives before Assign ends the run as CANCELLED without preparing the workspace. Idle wait. After a turn that ended normally with no queued prompt (and no complete_task, rate limit, budget limit, cancel or crash), the runtime reports AWAITING_INPUT and keeps the harness session up. A Prompt starts the next turn in the same session (reported as RUNNING), Cancel ends the run CANCELLED, and Release or the end of the wall-clock budget ends it END_TURN. If the turn had a blocking request (a ToolCallResult with await_input_after_turn, ask_question with blocking: true), Release ends the run BLOCKED instead; the budget end still gives END_TURN. complete_task in the same turn wins and ends the run COMPLETED. The runtime has no idle timer of its own: the control plane decides when to send Release (runs.keepAliveSeconds). A lost stream does not end the wait; the runtime reconnects. Shutdown. After the final RunReport is queued, the runtime keeps trying to deliver queued messages: it flushes them over the open stream, or reconnects with the usual backoff (also when the stream drops during the flush, for example by a control plane restart), until all are acknowledged or the final report flush window of 10 minutes has passed. Messages that are not acknowledged by then stay in the outbox and a warning is logged. main waits for the connection task for the window plus 60 s for a connection attempt that is under way. Git credentials. The runtime holds no Git credentials: the gateway’s Git proxy authenticates upstream. The generated .git/config sets an empty credential.helper (resets helpers from other config scopes) and http..sslCAInfo to the instance CA, scoped to scheme://host:port/ of the workspace repo_url so other HTTPS remotes keep the system trust store; git runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, so a rejected request fails at once instead of prompting. credential.* and http.* entries from the repository or Workspace.git_config are dropped. Git retries. A clone, fetch or push whose output shows HTTP 503 (returned error: 503) or a connection error (Failed to connect to, Connection refused, Connection reset by peer, Empty reply from server, and mid-transfer Operation timed out, transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining, SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, Recv failure, was not closed cleanly) is retried up to 3 times. Only git’s own lines count, not remote: lines from the server. A 403 together with the gateway’s remote: df: unknown source (the gateway has no snapshot with the pod IP yet) is retried as well. Output with [remote rejected], [rejected], any other 403 or 502 (the forge rejected the proxy’s credential) is never retried, nor is any other failure (DNS errors included: the proxy host is a hostAliases entry). Before a push is retried the runtime reads the remote ref with git ls-remote; if it already has the pushed commit (the response was lost after the ref update), the push counts as successful. Lazy blob fetches of the blobless clone (during checkout) are not retried.

data: Dark Factory runs code that an AI agent writes and executes. The design assumes that the agent, the repository contents and everything the agent produces are untrusted, and puts the protection at the boundary of the sandbox instead of inside it.
data.humans#Humans: Users log in through OIDC (see Authentication); every page needs the role board-member. Sessions are server-side; the browser only holds an HTTP-only cookie. Agents cannot approve their own requests: approvals need a human, and the control plane applies the approved action itself.
data.identity#Identity:
Each sandbox pod gets its own short-lived certificate from cert-manager’s CSI driver, with the URI SAN spiffe://dark-factory/ns//pod//. The private key never lands in a Kubernetes Secret. The control plane accepts a connection only if the namespace is the sandbox namespace, the pod exists with that UID and the instance’s labels, and the connection comes from the pod’s IP, so a copied key is useless from anywhere else. The gateway identifies sandboxes by source pod IP through a registry the control plane pushes to it.
Every action of an agent is bound to its run: sandbox identity, run, task, persona and project decide which repository, branches, hosts and tools it may use.
data.known-limits#Known limits: Without Kata Containers the sandbox is a regular container on the node kernel. The egress proxy sees host names and TLS handshakes, not request contents (no TLS interception). An allowed host is allowed with every path. Network traffic that ignores the proxy settings is dropped by the NetworkPolicy and does not show in the live traffic view. Dark Factory is pre-MVP and has had no external security review.
data.principles#Principles: The sandbox is the blast radius. Inside its pod the agent may do anything. Protection covers what crosses the boundary: network traffic, Git pushes, messages to the control plane. No long-lived credentials in the sandbox. The forge credential never enters it: the Git proxy adds it on the way out, and the control plane calls the forge API itself. The only secret a sandbox holds is the harness credential (for example the Claude subscription token), delivered over the agent channel into memory, never through the pod spec or a file. Git is the only durable store for code. The task volume is a cache; the runtime regenerates the files it owns (.git/config, hooks path) before using the repository. Default deny on the network. A sandbox reaches the control plane, the gateway and nothing else unless a rule allows it. See Egress gateway. Every privileged change is audited. Egress rules, push policies, stops, cancellations, decisions on requests and every push attempt are recorded with the actor.
data.sandbox-isolation#Sandbox isolation: Layer Setting Runtime class Kata Containers microVM where configured (sandboxNamespace.runtimeClassName); without it the sandbox shares the node kernel Pod security The sandbox namespace enforces Pod Security restricted: non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped Kubernetes API No service account token (automountServiceAccountToken: false); the sandbox namespace holds no Secrets Network A generated NetworkPolicy per run: egress only to the control plane agent port, the gateway and allowed cluster services; no ingress; no DNS Images The runtime and the harness are mounted as read-only image volumes; no container daemon, no nested containers
data.what-is-trusted#What is trusted: Trusted Untrusted The control plane, the gateway, the migrate job The harness and every process it starts PostgreSQL, the Kubernetes API, cert-manager The repository contents, including .git, hooks and configuration files The humans with the board-member role Everything on the task volume at the start of a run The forge, the model provider (as services, not their content) Tool output, web content and anything an agent sends to the control plane

data:
Sandboxes reach external hosts only through the gateway’s HTTPS proxy. The proxy enforces the egress rules per run and reports every connection to the live traffic view. Sandboxes resolve no DNS names themselves, which also closes DNS as an exfiltration channel.
flowchart LR S["Sandbox
HTTPS_PROXY = gateway IP"] -- "CONNECT host:443" --> P["Egress proxy"] P -- "source IP → run → rules" --> P P -- "allowed" --> H["api.anthropic.com, registries, …"] P -. "denied: 403, event" .-> L["Live traffic view"] CP["Control plane"] -- "PolicyWatch: registry + rules" --> P
data.limits#Limits: No path or method rules: an allowed host is allowed completely. Tools that ignore the proxy variables cannot reach external hosts at all; their attempts are dropped by the NetworkPolicy and do not appear in the live view. The source identity relies on the CNI preserving pod IPs for in-cluster traffic.
data.live-traffic#Live traffic: Each gateway pod keeps the latest connection events in memory (nothing is persisted per event).
